data.hook: Build your own ChatGPT in *13 lines*

scenes.text: A chatbot uses two kinds of instructions. [1] The system prompt, set by you, the builder. It defines the bot's personality, and rules, for the whole chat. [2] User messages, typed by the person, one at a time.

Here's a surprise. [1] The model has no memory between calls. Each call starts fresh. [2] So we keep a list of every message, the chat history. [3] And we send the whole history, every time, so the model sees the full conversation.

[1] Here's the code. [2] Set up the client, and an empty history list. [3] Loop forever. Read what the user types, and add it to the history, with the role user. [4] Call the model, with a system prompt that gives it a personality, and the full history. [5] Take the reply's text. [6] Add it to the history, as the assistant, and print it. [7] Now it remembers your name!

lines: system="You are a friendly AI tutor.",
output: AI: Namaste Ravi! What shall we learn?

scenes.text: Change one line, the system prompt, and you get a totally different bot. [1] A patient maths tutor, that never gives away the answer directly. [2] A support bot for your shop, that only talks about orders. [3] Or a Telugu speaking travel guide for Hyderabad.

Here's a common mistake. [1] Beginners let the history grow forever. [2] Every turn resends everything, so long chats get slower, cost more, and eventually overflow the context window. Real apps trim, or summarise, old messages.

data.myth: Just let the chat history grow forever.
data.fact: Long history costs more, runs slower, and can overflow the context window. Trim or summarise it.

data.question: A chatbot remembers because…
options: We resend the chat history every turn

scenes.text: Let's recap. [1] The system prompt sets personality and rules. [2] The model has no memory, so we keep a history list. [3] Every turn, we resend the full history. [4] And we trim long histories, to control cost. [5] Next, build RAG over your own PDFs. Follow AI Maastaaru!
